newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram confident of budget passage.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram confident of budget passage.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday that he was confident that parliament would approve the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.

"I am still hopeful that all political parties will find some way in which parliament can discharge its responsibility of passing the Finance Bill," he told reporters during a break in parliamentary debate over a motion of confidence in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Deve Gowda was expected to lose the vote of confidence, set for later on Friday, but his United Front coalition and Congress were holding talks to find a new leader and avert mid-term elections.
The finance minister said the speaker of the lower house, P.A. Sangma, had called a meeting of leaders of all political parties earlier on Friday to discuss the budget.
"As parliamentarians, it is possible to get together to pass the Finance Bill irrespective of the difficulties which the executive faces," Chidambaram said.
Officials said parliament might be asked to sit in a special session during the third week of April to discuss the budget and take a vote.
